entry.pin_map_check: The task text maps pin columns 3 boards apart (10-pin on 7, 7-pin on 33). Physically pins are 12 in apart, so columns are 6 in = 5.5 engine boards apart (10-pin ~3.5, 7-pin ~36.5). At 505 the ball sits on the 6-pin column: the 6 in map gives 8.0 against the edge read 8.4, the 3-board map gives 13.3. All pin_ruler reads here use the 6 in map.

method: Every path point was read by eye on gridded crops of the source frame (3x ball crops, 5.5-9x far-end zooms, 1.7x near lane zoom) made with cv2 from frames decoded by CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES (identical to sequential decode); lane edges are the wood end at the ball's own row in the same frame, with a Lab b* walker, an L-gradient snap (+-6 px) and an L profile used as aids that were checked against the crop, and at the pin rows the left edge is the end of the dark band before the 7-pin. board = 1 + 38 (x - right_x)/(left_x - right_x) at row y (left_x/right_x/board) and again at the contact row y+r (*_yr); min_board and hooks_back use the row-y column, the yr column agrees.
limits: Far end (495-510) the lane is 74-85 px wide, so 1 px is ~0.5 board; edges there are +-2-3 px (the row crosses the pin bodies and the left edge hides behind the 7-pin, read from a 4-8 px dark band) and ball centres +-1 px, so each far point is about +-1-1.5 boards and the 6.0->9.7 rise is 2-3x that. The pin ruler and the edges disagree on scale again (pins 9.8-10.25 px per 6 in imply a 70-72 px lane, edges give 74-80 px), so the pin-ruler reads sit 0.5-1 board below the edge reads; the rise from 503 to 509 shows in both (pin ruler 6.6 -> 9.5, edges 6.0 -> 9.9), but the pin ruler is not depth-free: a ball in front of the rack at a fixed off-centre board reads lower against the pin columns than it will at them (board lines converge to the VP), worth roughly 0.8-0.9 of its 2.9-board rise over the last ~4 ft; the edge reads carry no such term and still rise 2.6 (vs the 484-503 plateau) to 3.9 (vs the 503 dip). The move is not pin deflection: a ball on boards 8-10 can only clip the right side of the 3/6 pins, which would push it right, not left. Pins are still upright at 510-511 per loop 1, so the leftward move 503-509 is before contact, but a glancing 10-pin contact at 508-509 cannot be excluded from these frames. 448 and 460 edges are read on a rolled near-end view, +-5 px on a 220-510 px lane. Loop-1 'ball' points were used only as search seeds.
